authority: Registrar of Trade Unions, Labour Department, State Government

description.en: Registration of a Trade Union under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 enables workers to form and register a trade union with the Registrar of Trade Unions appointed by the state government. A minimum of 7 members (or 10% of the workers employed in the establishment, subject to a minimum of 7) are required to form and register a trade union. Registration confers legal status on the union, provides immunity from certain civil and criminal proceedings in relation to legitimate trade union activities, and enables the union to represent workers in collective bargaining, dispute resolution, and before labour courts.

verifiedConditions.claim: A minimum of 7 members are required to apply for registration of a trade union under Section 4 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926. For trade unions of workmen in an establishment, at least 10% of the workers or 7 workers (whichever is greater) must be members at the time of application.

Members of a trade union must be workers (persons employed in a trade or industry) or persons who were previously employed and are now unemployed. At least half of the office bearers must be persons actually engaged or employed in the industry with which the trade union is connected.

unverifiedEligibility: Workers below the age of 15 are generally not eligible to be members of a registered trade union.
Managerial and supervisory staff may form their own unions but typically cannot be members of a workmen's trade union.
Persons employed in the armed forces, police, and certain essential services may face restrictions on forming trade unions.
Employers can also form trade unions (employers' associations) under the Act.

requirements.claim: Application for registration in the prescribed form (Form A under Rule 2 of the Trade Unions Regulations) signed by at least 7 members of the trade union. The application must include the name and address of the trade union, the date of formation, and a statement of the objects of the union.

Copy of the rules of the trade union as required under Section 6 of the Act. The rules must cover: the name and objects of the union; purposes for which general funds may be spent; maintenance of member list; conditions for admission and expulsion of members; manner of amendment of rules; manner of dissolution; and provisions for audit of accounts.

List of members (at least 7 or 10% of workers, whichever is greater) with their names, addresses, occupations, and signatures or thumb impressions. The list must show that members are employed or were employed in the trade or industry.

Names, addresses, ages, and occupations of the office bearers (President, Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer, and other members of the executive committee) along with their consent to serve. At least half of the office bearers must be persons actually engaged or employed in the industry.

Resolution passed at the founding general body meeting authorizing the application for registration, adoption of the union's rules, and election of office bearers. Minutes of the founding meeting must be submitted.
Address of the registered office of the trade union where communications and notices may be addressed. Proof of address (rent agreement, utility bill, or NOC from the premises owner) is required.

Proof of collection of membership fee from members (receipt book or bank statement). A minimum subscription of Re 1 per month per member (for rural workers) or Rs 3 per month (for others) must be collected.
Identity proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID, or other government-issued ID) of all office bearers and the signatories of the application.

processInformation.appliesTo: Workers intending to form a trade union
processInformation.claim: Convene a general body meeting of at least 7 workers (or 10% of the workforce). Pass a resolution to form the trade union, adopt the rules of the union, elect office bearers, and authorize at least 7 members to sign the application for registration.

processInformation.appliesTo: Newly formed trade unions seeking registration
processInformation.claim: Submit the application in Form A along with the rules of the union, member list, office bearer details, founding meeting resolution, and registration fee to the Registrar of Trade Unions having jurisdiction over the registered office of the union.

The Registrar examines the application and documents for compliance with the Trade Unions Act and rules. If there are deficiencies, the Registrar may return the application with directions to rectify within a specified period. The Registrar may also seek verification from the employer regarding the employment status of the members.

If the Registrar is satisfied that the application complies with all requirements, the trade union is registered and a certificate of registration is issued. The Registrar enters the union's details in the register of trade unions maintained by the office. Registration must be granted or refused within 60 days of receipt of application.

output.claim: Certificate of Registration of Trade Union issued by the Registrar of Trade Unions under Section 9 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926. The certificate is conclusive evidence that the trade union has been duly registered. Registration provides the union with legal personality, ability to own property, enter contracts, sue and be sued, and immunity under Sections 17-19 of the Act for legitimate trade union activities.

fees.applicability: Registration fee for trade union registration
fees.claim: Registration fee varies by state, typically ranging from Rs 50 to Rs 500. The fee is payable along with the application. Some states also charge a nominal fee for amendment of rules or for issuing certified copies.

processingTime.applicability: From application submission to grant or refusal of registration
processingTime.claim: The Registrar must register the trade union or communicate the refusal within 60 days from the date of receipt of application. In practice, if the application is complete and compliant, registration may be granted within 15-30 days. If deficiencies are found, additional time is needed for rectification.

sources.title: The Trade Unions Act, 1926 (as amended)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Trade Unions Act, 1926 provides for the registration of trade unions and defines the law relating to registered trade unions. Section 4 requires a minimum of 7 members to apply for registration. Section 6 prescribes the matters that the rules of a trade union must provide for. Section 9 provides for the certificate of registration.
claimsSupported: Prescribed contents for trade union rules under Section 6.
Registration procedure and certificate under Section 9.
Immunities and legal protections for registered trade unions.
At least half the office bearers must be employed in the industry.
60-day timeline for Registrar to process the application.
sources.uncertainty: The Trade Unions Act is proposed to be subsumed under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020. State-specific rules and forms may vary. Registration fee amounts are set by state governments.

sources.title: Trade Unions — Ministry of Labour and Employment
sources.publisher: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Ministry of Labour and Employment provides information on the Trade Unions Act including registration procedures, rights and obligations of registered trade unions, and statistics on registered trade unions in India.
claimsSupported: Overview of trade union registration process.
Rights and privileges of registered trade unions.
Central and state government roles in trade union administration.
sources.uncertainty: The portal provides general information; state-specific procedures, forms, and fees must be verified with the respective state Labour Department.

limitations: Registration procedures, forms, and fees vary significantly across states as labour is a concurrent subject.
The Trade Unions Act 1926 is proposed to be subsumed under the Industrial Relations Code 2020; the new code has been enacted but notification of effective date is pending in most states.
The record covers the central Act provisions; state-specific trade union rules may impose additional requirements.
Registration does not confer recognition on the trade union for collective bargaining purposes; recognition is a separate process governed by state industrial relations laws.

The minimum membership requirement of 10% or 7 (whichever is greater) applies to trade unions of workmen in an establishment; general trade unions covering multiple establishments have different thresholds.
The Registrar has the power to cancel registration if the union's membership falls below the minimum or if the union obtained registration by fraud or mistake.
Office bearer eligibility rules (at least half must be from the industry) may be enforced differently across states.

review.reviewReason: Core Trade Unions Act provisions verified. State-specific procedures, fees, and the impact of the Industrial Relations Code 2020 need periodic monitoring.
nextReviewTrigger: Notification of the effective date of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 by central or state governments.
